pull.title: feat(observability): store the knobs, name the credential, measure the reasoning
pull.body:
# Observability that tells the truth: the knobs, the credential, and the measurement

The dashboard could not be trusted about the one thing it exists to report — what actually left this process. This fixes the writer, the reader, and the three places a NULL meant something different.

## What was wrong

Measured on a 204 MB copy of the live request log (10,242 requests / 74,126 attempts):

| | |
|---|---|
| attempts in one day with a stored wire body | 455 |
| of those, truncated | **212** |
| truncated previews still containing `reasoning_effort` | **0 / 212** |
| truncated previews still containing `temperature` / `top_p` | **0 / 212** |
| attempts with `reasoning_emitted = 0` under a non-suppressed adaptation | 148 |
| requests with a NULL `key_label` | 399 / 10,242 (62 of them with `key_index = 0`) |
| succeeded minimax attempts asked for reasoning | **3 of 6,614** — and it thought **0** times |
| succeeded hy3 attempts asked for reasoning | **0 of 977** — and it thought **977** times |

1. **The stored body was cut mid-string, and the cut landed on the knobs.** `summarize_wire_body` serialised with `sort_keys=True` and truncated at 8,000 characters, so a Claude Code request with ~59 tools spent the entire budget inside `tools` and every alphabetically later key fell off. What was stored was a cut JSON string under `_preview`, printed verbatim into a `<pre>`, unparseable by anything. The knobs were never actually lost — `params.wire` is not truncated and had them on 455/455 — the UI read three fields off it and discarded the rest.
2. **Gating and the wire contradicted each other in silence.** An adaptation reading *"enabling thinking and discarding effort 'max'"* sat beside a wire pane whose attempt had carried effort max, with nothing drawing the relation. The badge said "no reasoning sent", which reads as a fault — after #219 it is the correct outcome for a toggle-only model on an effort-only host.
3. **A request whose provider has no instrumented commit boundary showed no wire pane at all**, which reads as "no request body was sent".
4. **Attempts had no credential.** `requests.key_index`/`key_label` hold the last credential of the whole request, and the fully-benched path raised before recording one at all — so every benched-out request rendered as an ordinary keyless one.

## What to expect now

- **Every knob is stored, whole.** Non-content keys are emitted first and complete; only `messages`/`tools` degrade, to counts and names. The stored body always parses as JSON. The cap is now a setting: `REQUEST_LOG_WIRE_BODY_MAX_CHARS` (default 8000), and it bounds message/tool structure only.
- **A knobs block in the wire pane**, read from `params.wire`, so the knobs are legible even on a body stored by the old writer (`c-after-wire-knobs.png` — `reasoning_effort = max` beside a `<pre>` that never reaches the key).
- **Three honest states**: `reasoning sent: <value>`, `no reasoning instruction sent (model default applies)`, `reasoning not measured`. The pane is never hidden while a request has attempts (`c-after-not-measured.png`).
- **A contradiction badge** when the body carried nothing and gating had decided otherwise — keyed on a new `requests.reasoning_adaptation_kind` column carrying `ReasoningAdaptation.kind`, never on the message text (`c-after-contradiction.png`).
- **Per-attempt credentials** on `request_attempts`, rendered in the chain, with `(-1, "(no key available)")` for a fully benched pool.
- **A measured chip on the Models page**: "last 7d: reasoning requested X/N, returned Y/N" — two independent facts (`c-after-models-measured.png`).
- **One NULL convention**: a dash means not measured, a zero means measured and zero. `"keyless"` is gone; it invented a fact.

## Action required

None. Old rows keep their stored shape and render with their note; attempts written before the new columns show **"not measured"** and a dash, which is exactly what they are. Nothing is backfilled — rewriting stored bodies would fabricate data that was never captured.

## Known and deliberate

- **Attempt-level credential health is not shipped.** Measured at **109 ms** without `rotated_away` and **162 ms** with it on the 204 MB copy — affordable, but in this change it would land as a payload field with no rendered surface, and an unwired feature is worse than a missing one. Credential health stays request-level; the per-attempt truth is in the chain.
- **Request-level `reasoning_adaptation` still names one model while a fallback answered.** Moving it onto `request_attempts` is a schema and a gating-signature change.
- **Vertex has no commit boundary**, so its attempts are permanently "not measured". This makes that visible instead of hiding the pane.
- **Body redaction is by key name and credential shape**; a secret in an innocuous field with an unremarkable shape still survives.

## Verification

```
uv run ruff format --check .   # 982 files already formatted
uv run ruff check .            # All checks passed!
uv run ty check                # All checks passed!   (repo-wide)
```

Migration timed against a copy of the live 204 MB log: first construction with the two attempt ALTERs, the adaptation-kind ALTER and `idx_request_attempts_model_v1` **499 ms**, steady state **29 ms**. `reasoning_by_model(since=7d)` **130–170 ms**, cached for 5 s and run on a worker thread.

jsdom was available and ran (node 24), so the request-detail cases are driven through the real `admin.js`.

**Browser drive** (WORKING-NOTES §66): this worktree's `admin_static` served on `127.0.0.1:8099`, request-log endpoints answered from a **copy** of the live database by this branch's code (the running server is 5.73.0 and cannot return the new columns), Models payload proxied and augmented exactly as `_models_page_payload` does. The live server received loopback GETs only; nothing was written to `~/.fcc`. Observed:

- truncated glm-5.3-flash body → knobs block reads `reasoning_effort = max` while the `<pre>` beside it is the old cut string;
- minimax request with a DROPPED adaptation → **exactly one** contradiction badge across ten attempt panes, on the attempt that emitted nothing; the suppressed and kind-less cases badge nothing;
- minimax request with no instrumented attempt → pane visible, "Not measured" / "Never sent", chain credentials all dashes;
- Models page → `last 7d: reasoning requested 3/6614, returned 0/6614` on `commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free`;
- `list_console_messages` empty of errors and warnings on both pages.

## Residual risks

1. **Stored bodies can get larger.** Knobs are emitted whole even when they alone exceed the cap, so a pathological `extra_body` stores more than the setting's number suggests. Deliberate: a cut knob is unrecoverable, a cut turn list is not. The setting's description says what it bounds.
2. **Two body shapes coexist forever.** Rows written before this render as the legacy cut string with a note. No backfill.
3. **The measured chip is a rolling window** bounded by `REQUEST_LOG_MAX_ROWS`. A model whose traffic aged out shows no chip, which can look like "never measured" for a model that was heavily used. The chip names its window.
4. **`reasoning_by_model` joins two tables on every Models-page load.** Cached 5 s, indexed, off the event loop, and measured above — but unmeasured on a database far larger than 204 MB.
5. **Per-attempt attribution is only as good as the slot.** A provider that internally retries across keys inside one attempt still attributes that attempt to its last key. A smaller lie than the per-request one, not the absence of one.
6. **The contradiction badge depends on a column, not on prose** — which is the point — but it therefore fires on nothing at all for every row written before this release, and for any adaptation whose kind is `unchanged` or `suppressed`.

The local suite has **15 pre-existing failures** that also fail on unmodified `main` (8 websearch tests reading the real `~/.fcc/.env`, 6 PowerShell installer tests, and `tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`) — not introduced here.

commit.message:
feat(observability): store the knobs, name the credential, measure the reasoning

The dashboard could not be trusted about the one thing it exists to report:
what left this process. Four measurements, taken on a 204 MB copy of the live
log (10,242 requests / 74,126 attempts):

1. The stored wire body was cut mid-string, and the cut landed on the knobs.
   `summarize_wire_body` (core/wire_capture.py:345) serialised with
   `sort_keys=True` and truncated at 8,000 characters, so a Claude Code request
   with ~59 tools spent its whole budget inside `tools`. Of 455 attempts with a
   stored body in one day, 212 were truncated -- and `reasoning_effort`
   survived in **0 of 212**, `temperature`/`top_p` in **0 of 212**. What was
   stored under `_preview` was a cut JSON string, printed verbatim into a
   `<pre>` by `formatWireBody`, unparseable by anything.

   The knobs were never lost: `wire_params_summary` is not truncated and lands
   in `request_attempts.params.wire` on 455/455 of those attempts. The UI read
   three fields off it and discarded the rest, including `reasoning`.

2. Gating and the wire contradicted each other in silence. 148 attempts in one
   day had `reasoning_emitted = 0` under a non-suppressed adaptation, and the
   modal printed both as flat rows with no relation drawn -- an adaptation
   reading "enabling thinking and discarding effort 'max'" sat beside a wire
   pane whose sibling attempt had carried effort max. The wire badge said "no
   reasoning sent", which reads as a fault; after #219 it is the correct
   outcome for a toggle-only model on an effort-only host.

3. A request whose provider has no instrumented commit boundary showed no wire
   pane at all -- `renderWireRequest` filtered attempts on `wire_body` and hid
   the container -- which reads as "no request body was sent". 170 of 317
   succeeded minimax attempts in one day qualify.

4. `request_attempts` had no credential at all; `requests.key_index`/
   `key_label` hold the *last* credential of the whole request. 399/10,242
   requests had a NULL `key_label`, 62 of them with `key_index = 0` because the
   fully-benched path in `rotating.py` raises before `record_credential` ever
   runs and the baseline in `execution.py:576` had already claimed key 0 with
   `RotatingProvider.credential_label`, which is None. Every one of those
   rendered as an ordinary keyless request.

And no surface answered "does this model actually think": minimax was asked 3
times in 6,614 succeeded attempts and thought 0 times; hy3 was asked 0 times in
977 and thought 977 times.

What the surfaces say now
-------------------------

* The writer emits every non-content key **whole and first** (model, reasoning,
  sampling, extra_body, rest), then spends what is left of the budget on
  `messages` and `tools`, degrading them to counts and names. The output always
  parses as JSON; `_truncated`/`_preview` is never written again. The cap is a
  setting, `REQUEST_LOG_WIRE_BODY_MAX_CHARS` (default 8000), and its
  description says what it bounds.
* The wire pane gained a knobs block built from `params.wire`, so the knobs
  are readable even on a body stored by the old writer. The badge headlines the
  value that was carried, says "no reasoning instruction sent (model default
  applies)" when nothing was, and "reasoning not measured" when nobody was
  recording. The pane is never hidden while the request has attempts: an
  uninstrumented attempt says "Not measured", a skipped one says "Never sent".
* A contradiction badge fires when the body carried nothing and gating had
  decided otherwise. It keys on a new `requests.reasoning_adaptation_kind`
  column carrying `ReasoningAdaptation.kind` (#219 added the enum; nothing
  persisted it), **not** on a regex over the message: the message is prose that
  gets reworded, and a badge that reads a sentence fires or stops firing on an
  edit nobody connected to it. Rows written before the column badge nothing.
* `request_attempts` gained `key_index`/`key_label`, captured at the attempt
  boundary, and the chain renders one per attempt. A fully benched pool now
  records the sentinel `(-1, "(no key available)")` instead of leaving the
  request attributed to key 0 with no label.
* The Models page gained a measured chip per model: "last 7d: reasoning
  requested X/N, returned Y/N", from a new `RequestLogStore.reasoning_by_model`
  covered by `idx_request_attempts_model_v1`. Requested and returned are
  independent measurements and both are shown.
* One NULL convention across the modal, the chain, the websearch credential
  table and the analytics breakdowns: a dash means not measured, a zero means
  measured and zero. `"keyless"` is gone -- it invented a fact.

Non-obvious choices
-------------------

* `DEFAULT_WIRE_BODY_MAX_CHARS` lives in `core/wire_capture.py` and
  `config/constants.py` mirrors the literal, because `core` may not import
  `config`; a test pins the two together rather than letting them drift.
* The knobs are emitted whole even when they alone exceed the limit. A cut knob
  is the defect being fixed; a body that exceeds its cap because `extra_body`
  is enormous is a bounded, visible cost.
* `reasoning_by_model` shares `stats()`'s cache and TTL, and the Models route
  floors its `since` to the minute -- with a raw `time.time()` the key would
  miss the cache on every single page load.
* The attempt-level credential breakdown (spec §4.5) is **not** shipped; see
  below.

Verification
------------

`uv run ruff format --check` (982 files), `uv run ruff check`, repo-wide
`uv run ty check`, and the full `uv run pytest -q`. jsdom was available and ran
(node 24): the request-detail cases are driven through the real `admin.js`.
Migration timed against a copy of the live 204 MB log: first construction with
the three ALTERs and the new index 499 ms, steady state 29 ms;
`reasoning_by_model(7d)` 130-170 ms, cached 5 s.

Driven in Chrome against this worktree's `admin_static` served on 127.0.0.1:8099
with the request log read from a copy of the live database (the running server
is 5.73.0 and cannot return the new columns; it received loopback GETs only and
nothing was written to ~/.fcc):

* a truncated glm-5.3-flash body -- knobs block reads `reasoning_effort = max`
  while the `<pre>` beside it is the old cut string that never reaches the key;
* a minimax request with a DROPPED adaptation -- exactly one contradiction
  badge across ten attempt panes, on the attempt that emitted nothing;
* a minimax request with no instrumented attempt -- pane visible, "Not
  measured" and "Never sent" as appropriate, chain credentials all dashes;
* the Models page -- "last 7d: reasoning requested 3/6614, returned 0/6614" on
  minimax;
* no console errors or warnings on either page.

Deliberately not done
---------------------

* **Attempt-level credential health.** Measured at 109 ms without
  `rotated_away` and 162 ms with it on the 204 MB copy -- affordable, but it
  would land as a payload field with no rendered surface in this change, and an
  unwired feature is worse than a missing one. Credential health stays
  request-level; the per-attempt truth is in the chain.
* **Request-level `reasoning_adaptation` names one model while a fallback
  answered.** Moving the adaptation onto `request_attempts` is a schema and a
  gating-signature change.
* **Vertex commit boundary.** `providers/vertex/` has no `record_wire_request`
  call, so its attempts are permanently "not measured". This makes that
  visible rather than hiding the pane.
* **Body redaction by pattern.** `redact_wire_value` redacts by key name and
  credential shape; a secret in an innocuous field with an unremarkable shape
  still survives.
* **No backfill.** Bodies stored by the old writer keep `_truncated`/`_preview`
  and render with their note; rewriting them would fabricate data.
